themes_detail.label: Street/Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 42 THIS WEEK versus an 8-week average of 11.8 per week—a 257% increase (z-score: 5.75)—suggesting a new localized noise source or event affecting outdoor spaces in Crown Heights.
evidence: 42 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.8 weekly average (257% increase, z-score: 5.75)
Commercial noise also up 113% THIS WEEK (42 complaints vs. 19.8 weekly average, z-score: 4.72)
Combined noise signals suggest acute, neighborhood-wide disturbance
reporting_angles: Investigate what new construction, street event, or commercial activity began this week that triggered the spike
Interview residents on specific streets where complaints cluster; document noise sources and times of day

themes_detail.label: Traffic & Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints jumped 600% THIS WEEK (7 complaints vs. 1.0 weekly average, z-score: 6.0) and street condition complaints jumped 300% (43 THIS WEEK vs. 10.8 weekly average, z-score: 4.17)—indicating a rapid deterioration of street infrastructure or a traffic incident affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Traffic complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (600% increase, z-score: 6.0, severity: high)
Street condition complaints: 43 THIS WEEK vs. 10.8 weekly baseline (300% increase, z-score: 4.17, severity: high)
Dangling street signs also spiked 1020% last week (7 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 avg), suggesting ongoing street infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints spatially to identify if spike is localized to a single corridor or dispersed; visit sites to document pothole, curb, or traffic signal damage
Contact NYC DOT to ask if there was an incident (water main break, accident, construction closure) that triggered this week's surge

themes_detail.label: Graffiti & Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped 465% THIS WEEK (12 complaints vs. 2.1 weekly average, z-score: 4.73), while illegal dumping rose 173% LAST WEEK (14 complaints vs. 5.1 weekly average, z-score: 4.03)—a converging signal of declining neighborhood cleanliness and possible enforcement gaps.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 12 THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (465% increase, z-score: 4.73, severity: high)
Illegal dumping: 14 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average (173% increase, z-score: 4.03, severity: high)
Both signal a rapid breakdown in street sanitation; suggests possible pause in enforcement or influx of unauthorized activity
reporting_angles: Photograph graffiti and dumping hotspots; ask Sanitation and NYPD if they reduced patrols or if a specific building/site is the source
Interview community board members about enforcement priorities; check if there's a backlog in graffiti removal or illegal dumping enforcement

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged 567% LAST WEEK (5 complaints vs. 0.8 weekly average, z-score: 5.13)—a statistically significant spike suggesting unauthorized tree cutting, limb damage, or environmental crime in the district.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score: 5.13, severity: high)
Parks Department budget requests include 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park,' suggesting ongoing park infrastructure challenges
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to identify which trees or parks were damaged and whether this is linked to a single incident or multiple actors
Walk Prospect Park and major residential streets to document tree condition and interview residents about what they witnessed

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise & Activity Expansion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints more than doubled THIS WEEK (42 complaints vs. 19.8 weekly average, 113% increase, z-score: 4.72), coinciding with a street/sidewalk noise surge—suggesting new commercial operations, a venue opening, or expanded nightlife activity in the district.
evidence: Commercial noise: 42 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.8 weekly average (113% increase, z-score: 4.72, severity: high)
Street/sidewalk noise also surged 257% simultaneously, suggesting shared underlying cause (event, construction, or new venue)
516 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (319 alterations) indicates active commercial build-out in district
reporting_angles: Cross-reference recent DOB permits and 311 complaints by address to identify which new business or construction project is driving noise
Interview residents in highest-complaint blocks; check SLA database for recent liquor license applications or renewals
